title: What If You Bought Every Lottery Ticket? In 1992 a Group Tried

scenes.text: What if you bought every possible lottery ticket? In 1992, a group of investors actually tried.
Virginia's jackpot had hit 27 million dollars. The game had only about 7.1 million possible combinations.
So an Australian syndicate set out to buy them all, handing shops stacks of ten thousand pre-filled slips.
Time ran out. By the draw on February fifteenth, they held about 5.5 million. Over a million gaps remained.
The winning numbers were among theirs. The lottery investigated, found no rule broken, and paid the jackpot.
Then Virginia tightened its rules on block sales. Even buying almost everything, they had still needed luck.

description:
What if you bought every possible lottery ticket? In February 1992 an Australian syndicate set out to buy all of the roughly 7.1 million six-number combinations in Virginia's Lotto, whose jackpot stood at 27 million dollars.
They ran out of time and held about 5.5 million combinations at the 15 February draw, but the winning one was among them. Virginia's lottery ruled the ticket had been bought within the rules and awarded the jackpot, then met to tighten its regulations on block sales.
